stories.title: Uruguay plans 99 MW solar tender with 20-year PPAs
stories.description: Uruguay’s state-owned power utility will procure electricity from three privately developed solar plants, each with 33 MW of grid injection capacity, under long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs).

stories.title: Saft opens solid-state battery production line in France
stories.description: Saft, a subsidiary of TotalEnergies, has inaugurated a production line at its Bordeaux facility to develop and manufacture solid-state batteries, targeting aviation and space applications with energy density up to 50% higher than conventional lithium-ion technology, according to the company.

stories.title: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
stories.description: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Until recently, you could divide internet users into just two categories: bots and people.

stories.title: The Download: preserving the Arctic permafrost, and playful AI agents
stories.description: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

stories.title: AI assistant startup Town nabs unicorn valuation 4 months after launch
stories.description: AI assistant startup Town nabbed a unicorn valuation on Monday, announcing a $108 million Series B round co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures.

stories.title: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs
stories.description: Nvidia is leaning hard into the trend of enterprise companies wanting to run their own open models in their own data centers and also trying to make on-device, private AI agents a thing.

stories.title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?
stories.description: Ahead of the midterms Trump has boasted about the performance of the US economy. BBC Verify looks at inflation, jobs and economic growth in the country.

stories.title: EU tariffs aimed at China hitting Ukraine, steel boss says
stories.description: The boss of one of Ukraine's biggest steel companies says the country has been "bundled together" in measures aimed at curbing cheap imports.

stories.title: Scientists win 2026 Nobel Prize for controlling brain cells with light
stories.description: A discovery in tiny algae led to a Nobel Prize-winning breakthrough that allows scientists to switch brain cells on and off using light. The revolutionary technique has already helped researchers activate memories and is opening new possibilities for restoring vision and treating brain disorders.

stories.title: Just 3,000 steps a day may help slow Alzheimer's, scientists find
stories.description: Walking just 3,000 steps a day could help slow Alzheimer’s-related brain changes, according to new research. Scientists discovered that physical activity was linked to less buildup of harmful tau proteins and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline, even in people already showing early signs of the disease.

stories.title: Dominican Republic to introduce grid usage fee for distributed PV
stories.description: Dominican Republic utility Edesur will introduce a new grid usage charge for certain solar net metering customers from Nov. 1, 2026. The charge will apply to electricity exported to the grid, although questions remain over which existing contracts will be affected.

stories.title: A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub
stories.description: Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor. To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea. Three fabs already operate around the clock, and a fourth is coming online.
